title: You may now qualify for Google’s new Search profile, here’s how to check
summary: Google has lowered the follower requirements and appears ready to expand Search profiles globally.
body: TL;DR Google has lowered Search profile requirements to 35,000 followers on YouTube, Instagram, and X, and 100,000 on TikTok. Search profiles are already appearing outside the US, even though Google’s support page still lists the US as the only supported market. Google says it plans to expand the feature further and has “more to come” for creators. If you have ever wished Google Search could give your favorite creators or publishers something closer to a social media profile, Google is getting there. The company launched Search profiles in June , giving eligible publishers and creators a dedicated space to bring their websites, social accounts, videos, and posts together. Now, Google is making those profiles considerably easier to get. Google’s Search profiles initially required a sizable following: 100,000 followers on YouTube, Instagram, or X, or 300,000 on TikTok. Google has now lowered those thresholds to 35,000 for YouTube, Instagram, and X, while TikTok’s requirement drops to 100,000 followers.

title: More Pixel 11 phones now have this NFC payments upgrade
summary: There is one major exception, though.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google has quietly confirmed that all Pixel 11 Pro Fold models support the FeliCa contactless standard. It also looks like all Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro models outside the US support this standard. FeliCa is a contactless standard that’s popular in Japan for payments and transit. NFC is a staple on most Android phones today, allowing you to easily make wireless payments. However, Japan has its own wireless payment solution dubbed FeliCa, which requires dedicated hardware in the phone. The good news is that Pixel 11 phones now offer much better support for this standard. Google’s support page reveals (thanks, Dylan H!) that the Pixel 11 Pro Fold supports FeliCa globally. Furthermore, the page shows that Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro models outside the US also support FeliCa.

title: PSA: Don’t trust that Chrome update popup — it could be malware
summary: A suspicious extension appears to be triggering convincing fake browser update warnings.
body: TL;DR Persistent pop-ups urging you to update Chrome may actually be malware pushed by compromised browser extensions. The issue affects Chromium-based browsers like Chrome, Brave, and Opera, attempting to trick users into running potentially malicious scripts. Identifying and removing suspicious or newly acquired extensions is currently the primary way to stop the pop-ups. We all have our favorite Chrome extensions that make daily web browsing effortless, whether it’s a quick screen snip tool, a right-click unlocker, or a simple tab manager. But what happens when one of those trusty add-ons quietly turns against you? Over the past few days, an increasing number of web users have fallen victim to a frustratingly convincing browser scam that tricks people into downloading harmful malware disguised as routine system updates. The issue manifests as an aggressive pop-up claiming a “Critical Update Required” or “Update available” to keep using your browser. If you click to proceed, instead of a standard browser update, it downloads a suspicious .vbs or .exe script directly to your machine.

title: Forget Flock — this system could let police track your car with help from your phone
summary: SignalTrace can link devices to vehicles.
body: TL;DR Leonardo US Cyber and Security Solutions is proposing its SignalTrace tech to law-enforcement agencies. SignalTrace could let police track vehicles using the electronic signals from phones, laptops, smartwatches, and other nearby devices alongside ALPR cameras. While Leonardo says the system does not identify individuals, recurring device signatures could potentially be linked to specific vehicles and their registered owners. The technology could help police track vehicles that evade license-plate cameras, but it could also flag innocent people when their devices appear in vehicles associated with an investigation. Imagine a world where the police can identify people on the move not just by their license plate, but also the electronic devices that are traveling with them. This is exactly what a new sensor system from Leonardo US Cyber and Security Solutions is designed to achieve. The technology is aptly named SignalTrace, and it is designed to detect Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and RFID signals being emitted from nearby devices (via ArsTechnica ). Leonardo’s idea is to deploy these sensors alongside automatic license plate recognition (ALPR) cameras like those from Flock.

title: The RAM crisis might be forcing manufacturers to cut corners you can hear
summary: Your next phone could sound worse.
body: TL;DR Rising RAM costs are forcing phone makers to make difficult tradeoffs to avoid raising prices. Xiaomi’s 17T appears to have cut costs on its speakers, with testing showing weaker audio than its predecessor. As manufacturers look for savings, buyers may need to dig deeper than the spec sheet to spot hidden compromises. The rising RAM cost crisis isn’t letting up anytime soon, and manufacturers are increasingly being forced to make tradeoffs just to keep phone prices from climbing even higher. Motorola, for example, took the stagnation route by using the same chipset in the Razr Ultra 2026 as in its predecessor . Stagnation is still somewhat understandable, especially when the chip in question is the Snapdragon 8 Elite. Xiaomi, on the other hand, could potentially be taking a completely different approach. The company released the Xiaomi 17T late in May. The device is positioned as a mid-range alternative to flagships, and hence, Xiaomi presumably wanted to maintain its modest price tag. But the manufacturer reportedly did so by making a compromise that isn’t immediately evident when looking at spec sheets.

body: It wasn’t too long ago that practically every Android phone had a dedicated, multicolor notification LED . Usually placed above the display, the glowing light was surprisingly useful for notifying you of messages, alerts, charging levels, and other things you needed to be aware of. As a self-proclaimed fan of notification LEDs, I loved being able to glance at my phone from a distance and tell if I needed to take action. Always-on displays on phones can replicate some of that functionality, but they’re nowhere near as discreet as a simple light. No wonder then that Android fans have been clamoring for the return of the notification LED. As we’ve seen time and time again, design innovation tends to be cyclical. title: The Pixel 11 Pro officially says goodbye to the thermometer after three generations
summary: Google's swapping the temperature sensor for the HiLight LED.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NKVHYtQlCb8 TL;DR Google has confirmed that its Pixel 11 Pro phones no longer offer a temperature sensor. The new phones now have the so-called HiLight notification LED in place of the thermometer. Google first introduced the temperature sensor on the Pixel 8 Pro in 2023. The Pixel 8 Pro debuted a thermometer or temperature sensor back in 2023. This rear-facing sensor allowed you to (surprise) measure the temperature of objects and eventually people. However, the Pixel 11 Pro phones all offer the so-called HiLight feature in the camera bar, so what does this mean for the temperature sensor? Google has confirmed to Android Authority that none of the Pixel 11 series devices have a thermometer:

title: I spent two hours with the Pixel 11 series. Here’s what blew me away — and what went wrong
summary: Plus the Pixel Watch 5 and Pixel Tag, too.
body: Google fans, gather around. After enduring months of leaks, the wait for the Pixel 11 series is finally over. The Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold are all official, and you can pre-order them all right now. It’s one thing to look at the new phones on the Google Store website or read news articles about them, but actually using them for yourself is completely different. Thankfully, I had a chance to spend a couple of hours with all of the new Pixel 11 models , and I came away with a few important takeaways I think you should know about.

title: Pixel 11 camera comes with built-in teleprompter and timeline for your content creator needs
summary: Google built a mini video editing bay inside Pixel 11's Camera app.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NKVHYtQlCb8 TL;DR Google is adding new tools for video creators to the Pixel 11’s Camera app. These include a teleprompter and basic video editing tools, right within the Camera app. Pixel 11 will also organize video clips into project albums automatically. There’s no doubting that video creators (or even users who take a lot of videos) gravitate toward the iPhone . That stays true, even if certain top-tier options in the Android camp might offer better video recording capabilities , and that’s something Google may now be attempting to change. However, instead of taking on the iPhone simply with better video quality, Google is pitching extra features that may come in handy for those who shoot videos with the Pixel 11. With the Pixel 11, Google is adding a new set of tools that allow video creators to channel their creativity with more ease. These features are grouped under what Google calls “Creator Suite,” and they make video creation easier, especially when using the front camera.

title: Pixel 11 takes on iPhone’s Photographic Styles with Camera Looks, including retro film filters
summary: You can finally ditch the ultra-processed look on your Pixel photos.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NKVHYtQlCb8 TL;DR With the Pixel 11, Google is introducing Camera Looks, which lets users tune how their images look. Users can choose from a range of looks, from ultra-detailed to soft, muted aesthetics, which they can also customize. Along with these, Pixel 11 also brings film-inspired camera filters for a retro look. A complaint with modern phone cameras that more and more people have is about the excessive digital processing that images go through. This has resulted in more and more users yearning for camera apps that deliver photos with minimal or no processing . Google seems to be incorporating that feedback for its newly launched Pixel 11 series, and giving users control over how processed they want their images to be — along with a host of film-inspired camera filters. With Pixel 11, Google brings what it calls Camera Looks, which includes distinct color filters that you can apply to your photos. The new feature, which appears to be Google’s take on the iPhone’s Photographic Styles, lets you choose among the following four styles:

title: Google Pixel 11 cases finally let the phone colors shine through
summary: Google is expanding Pixelsnap with a clear case, a hinge-protecting Fold case, and more colorful Ring Stand options.
body: TL;DR Google has introduced clear Pixelsnap cases for the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, and Pixel 11 Pro XL. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold gets a dedicated case with an integrated hinge cover for extra protection. The Pixelsnap Ring Stand is now available in Canyon, Olive, and Obsidian, alongside the existing Moonstone option. Pixelsnap cases and accessories debuted with the Pixel 10 series last year and were among the more obvious add-ons for buyers of the 2025 Google handsets. But there was a minor trade-off, because you could protect your new phone or show off its color , but not really both. Google is fixing that with the Pixel 11 series, introducing a new clear case alongside updated colored cases and a more protective option for the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. The Pixelsnap Clear Case is available for the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, and 11 Pro XL. It uses TPU and polycarbonate, with built-in magnets for Pixelsnap accessories and Qi2 charging. Depending on the model, the case weighs between 30.8g and 34g, but the Pixel 11 Pro Fold misses out on the transparent option.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro Fold can turn sign language into text, here’s how
summary: It's a useful new feature for sign language users.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NKVHYtQlCb8 TL;DR The Pixel 11 Pro Fold supports transcribing American Sign Language (ASL) into text. It uses the front camera to see what the user is signing, and displays the translation on the cover screen as well. The feature currently only supports ASL and is available in select countries and regions. Google today announced the Pixel 11 series , including its newest foldable: the Pixel 11 Pro Fold . While it’s easy to get distracted by the foldable Pixel’s sleek design and new 48MP camera, the phone also comes with a feature that could prove to be very useful. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold supports transcribing American Sign Language to text. The phone will use its camera to see and understand ASL gestures and transcribe them into text directly on the screen. This could make it easier for ASL users to communicate with others, even if they don’t know sign language.

Google has just unveiled the Pixel 11 series , so should we expect the new tech here as well? Unfortunately, Google told Android Authority that the Pixel 11 phones don’t have silicon-carbon batteries:

title: Pixel 11’s Magic Capture promises you’ll never miss the shot (or the moment)

body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NKVHYtQlCb8 TL;DR Pixel 11 brings new camera features, including Magic Capture, which captures photos and videos automatically and gives you the best shots and clips. Magic Capture uses Gemini to pick the top five images and one video clip, emphasizing the best features. The feature is currently limited to the Pixel 11 phones, and Google hasn’t revealed plans to bring it to the older ones. The Pixel 11 series has just landed , and it feels quite identical to the last generation, save for minor external changes. Google relies almost entirely on software features, but there are some seemingly useful ones that could make the Pixel 11 look like a worthy upgrade. One of them is Magic Capture, which should spare you the trouble of finding the perfect frames for photos and videos during important moments. Instead of fidgeting with framing, and thus living life through the viewfinder, you can be present in those moments while letting the Pixel 11 take care of recording them. Google describes Pixel 11’s new Magic Capture as the means to “catch the moment while you live.” It captures photos and videos simultaneously and later presents you with a bunch of opti…

title: Google Pixel 11 series introduces new ‘Extreme Charging Mode’
summary: The new setting prioritizes system resources on power delivery to help users get a quick top-up when needed.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NKVHYtQlCb8 TL;DR Google has introduced a new “Extreme Charging Mode” across the Pixel 11 lineup, designed to focus device performance strictly on charging for fast battery boosts. The company hasn’t shared specifics on how this mode works or how much charge you can expect before your phone throttles its charging speed. Standard battery charging times (wired) remain largely unchanged, though all Pixel 11 models now support 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging. Google Pixel phones aren’t the fastest-charging phones out there, but the company has made some progress over the years, ensuring its phones aren’t at the bottom of the pack, at least. With the new Pixel 11 series , Google is blessing the phones with a new Extreme Charging Mode. Google hasn’t shared details yet, but it says you can turn on Extreme Charging Mode to “focus your phone’s performance entirely on powering up.” This way, users can get an “ultra-fast boost” when they need it the most. We’ll be putting all the phones through their paces to figure out what this mode does exactly, and just how much of a difference it would make to the wired charging experience.

title: Pixel 11 Pro phones get Pro Stable Video mode, but there’s a huge limitation
summary: The Pixel 11 Pro line's new video mode has a major weakness compared to similar modes on rival phones.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DvjtwGVAw1I TL;DR Google’s Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL now offer a Pro Stable Video recording mode. This mode activates automatically in shaky, brightly lit scenes, delivering smoother, more stable video clips. Google told Android Authority that this mode is part of Video Boost, which means it doesn’t work without an internet connection. Google has finally launched the Pixel 11 series of phones, and there’s no shortage of notable features. In fact, one of the new additions this year seems ideal if you want smoother, more stabilized video capture. The Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel Pro XL both offer a Pro Stable Video mode. At first glance, this seems to be Google’s answer to Super Steady, Ultra Stable, and Action modes seen on rival phones. This mode offers improved stabilization and smoother video compared to the default and Active stabilization modes. Google adds that Pro Stable Video mode activates automatically in shaky, bright-lit scenes. That should take some of the legwork out of capturing smooth video clips.

title: Google’s Pixel Glow is officially HiLight, but only Pro Pixels are getting it
summary: Buying a Pro Pixel 11? You'll now know who's calling and what Gemini is doing without touching your screen.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DvjtwGVAw1I TL;DR Google has officially named the Pixel 11 Pro’s rumored Pixel Glow feature “HiLight.” It’s an array of ambient LED lights built around the camera’s flash. HiLight can use custom colors to alert you when a favorite contact calls, including calls made through Phone by Google and WhatsApp. The LEDs also react to Gemini and could eventually handle more alerts, with Google already planning to add message notifications from Favorite Contacts. After months of leaks that left little to the imagination, Google has finally unveiled its Pixel 11 flagship lineup , along with the official name of one of its most-rumored new features. For months, we knew it as Pixel Glow, a name I personally preferred, but with the launch of the Pixel 11 series, we now know Google is calling it HiLight. Exclusive to the Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold , HiLight is essentially a small array of ambient LEDs around the camera flash. It is designed to give you information without requiring you to turn over or unlock your phone.

title: Pixel Watch 5’s At a Glance is more convenient than ever
summary: It'll pop up on the bottom of your watch's screen when you need it.
body: TL;DR Along with the Pixel 11 series, Google formally announced the Pixel Watch 5 at its hardware event today. The new watch comes with an updated take on At a Glance, which automatically surfaces various information depending on your personal context. The new version of the feature appears at the bottom of the watch’s screen when needed and can be expanded with a hands-free gesture. At a Glance is getting an upgrade on the new Pixel Watch 5 . While previous Pixel Watch models have offered an At a Glance watch face complication , the new generation Google finally unveiled today can surface relevant, glanceable info on your watch’s home screen regardless of which watch face you’ve chosen or which complications you’ve added. The new wearable version of At a Glance shows up at the bottom of the Pixel Watch 5’s display, in the same spot you’d see indicators for things like unread notifications or ongoing exercise tracking. What pops up there and when is situational, and Google says it can be as specific and real-time as a countdown of stops left on your public transit route until you need to get off.

title: Pixel 11’s At a Glance wants to tell you what’s good at restaurants
summary: Or what Maps users say is good, at least.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DvjtwGVAw1I TL;DR Google announced new At a Glance capabilities at its Pixel 11 event today. On the new Pixel phones, At a Glance can surface store loyalty cards and info about restaurants you visit. These features are currently in preview and will be available in low-density areas at first. At a Glance is one of Google’s best Pixel-exclusive software features, proactively surfacing relevant info — changes in the weather, upcoming appointments, ongoing timers, and more — in easy-to-see spots on your phone’s home and lock screens. With the Pixel 11 series , Google has announced new At a Glance features that could save you some tapping at restaurants and stores. On Pixel 11, At a Glance will be able to use your phone’s location data to know when you’re at a restaurant to proactively give you recommendations about what to order, or to know when you’re at a store to provide quick access to relevant loyalty cards. The feature is “in preview,” though, so you can probably expect some rough edges.

title: Google Maps could soon make it easy to clean up your list clutter
summary: With a single-tap control to hide or show your pins for saved places on the map.
body: Credit: Akshay Gangwar / Android Authority TL;DR Google is testing a new option to hide all your saved places from the map view with a single tap. This could be accomplished through a consolidated “All saved places” superlist that could combine all saved places under a single roof. Google is also testing an option to simplify how you discuss specific lists using Ask Maps. Google Maps has become an indispensable part of our commute, and countless mobile phone users rely on it frequently. Among the many nifty features it offers, Google Maps lets you save places of importance or interest, such as the ones you’d like to visit , and you can even compile these into a list. These saved places are cataloged on Google Maps’ You tab, and also show up in the actual map view when you’re scanning the nearby area. If you don’t want your saves crowding up the map, you can also hide them, but the option currently requires you to hide them per list. To make the process a bit easier, Google is now testing an option to hide all your saved places from the map view at once.

title: HONOR Robot Phone hands-on: I can’t believe it actually works this well!
summary: After ten months of teases, we're finally getting to experience a smartphone that's built unlike any other.
body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kCAdTV7M25c It’s one thing to be following along with the development of the latest smartphone in your favorite series — maybe like one of the new Pixel 11 models debuting today. Rumors may go back and forth on specs over the months leading up to launch, but even just going into it, you probably have a solid idea of the sort of device to expect. But then there are the phones that really attempt to do something all-new, and the path these take to market can prove a whole lot more interesting. For the better part of a year now, going all the way back to last October, HONOR has been teasing a smartphone with a camera unlike any other: the Robot Phone. Instead of a camera fixed in place to the back of the handset like you’ll see almost everywhere else, the Robot Phone’s camera is on the end of an articulated gimbal arm, like you may be familiar with from cameras like DJI’s Osmo Pocket series.

title: Verizon is so fed up with cable vandals, it’s putting a $25,000 bounty on them
summary: Verizon faced network outage related issues earlier this week due to acts of vandalism.
body: TL;DR Verizon will give away $25,000 to anyone who provides information leading to the arrest of vandals who damaged the carrier’s network infrastructure. This follows widespread incidents of vandalism and theft in the recent past, which led to a service outage earlier this week. More than half of the reported incidents come from California and Texas, according to recent data. Earlier this week, Verizon confirmed that vandalism of fiber cables caused widespread disruptions to mobile and internet services across parts of Southern California and Los Angeles. While the carrier said at the time that law enforcement was brought in to investigate these incidents, it is now seeking the community’s help to identify the vandals. In a blog post , Verizon says it will offer a $25,000 reward to people who provide information about the vandals, provided it leads to an arrest and conviction. As the carrier points out, such disruptions can lead to devastating outcomes for sectors that rely on continuous access to mobile/internet services, such as healthcare and emergency response services.

title: This shocking Zoom bug allowed silent device takeovers on Android and iOS
summary: A zero-click bug allowed attackers to silently take control during live Zoom calls.
body: TL;DR A Zoom annotation flaw could let a malicious participant remotely take over another person’s device without any interaction. Researchers found and exploited the bug using publicly available AI models in fewer than 20 prompts. Zoom has patched the flaws, so updating the Zoom app is the most important thing you can do. Over the past few months, we have watched frontier AI models rapidly alter the cybersecurity landscape — from AI models breaking technical barriers to mounting regulatory scrutiny over weaponized AI capabilities . Now, a newly disclosed Zoom flaw shows just how serious that can become. Researchers used undisclosed publicly available AI models to uncover a vulnerability that could have allowed someone on a Zoom call to take control of another participant’s device. The flaw affected Zoom clients on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android. Worse, the attack required no click, download, or other action from the victim. Simply being in the same meeting could be enough.
